entry.idea: Greenly automatically calculates a company's carbon footprint from its financial and operational data, so businesses can track and report emissions without doing the accounting by hand.
entry.lesson: Buying a competitor outright can be faster than out-building them when a market is consolidating around a handful of platforms doing the same job.
entry.name: Greenly

growth.reason: It serves about 2,000 companies and just acquired a direct competitor for €65 million, a clear sign of scale and market consolidation.

market.reason: Carbon emissions reporting is becoming a mandatory requirement for large companies across many countries and industries, a large and growing compliance market.

tech.reason: It automates emissions calculations from a company's financial and operational data, solid data engineering rather than a hard scientific barrier.

sources.title: Greenly acquires Normative in carbon accounting consolidation
French carbon accounting startup Greenly raises €48M funding to accelerate adoption of emissions reporting - Silicon Canals
How This French Startup Is Helping Companies Clean Up Their Carbon Clutter With $75 Million - Forbes

entry.twist: It recently acquired a direct competitor, Normative, for €65 million, consolidating two carbon accounting platforms into one to serve a much larger combined customer base.
entry.who_pays: Large companies across Europe and the US, including brands like LVMH, L'Oréal and TripAdvisor, pay to use Greenly's platform to track and reduce their carbon footprint.
entry.why_now: New regulations are forcing more companies worldwide to measure and report their carbon emissions, and manually calculating those numbers is too slow and error-prone to keep up with demand.
